name: Gaza Marine–El Arish Offshore Gas Pipeline
monitor_reason: Threshold leg (c) fails at the pipeline level. Legs (a) sponsor [EGAS 45% operator, PIF 27.5%, CCC 27.5%] and (b) endpoints [Gaza Marine field -> El Arish, Egypt] are met, but there is no concrete step specific to THIS pipeline. The MoU (Feb 2021), Framework Agreement (Oct 2022) and Israeli preliminary approval (June 2023) all pertain to the upstream Gaza Marine FIELD development consortium, not to a committed pipeline (no pipeline FEED/EPC award, permit, tender, or FID). The El Arish subsea route is only one competing commercialization option (vs Israel's Ashdod), and the whole scheme has been dormant since Oct 2023 with no infrastructure work; as of Aug 2025 nothing has commenced. Pipeline is a routing concept tied to a stalled, never-developed field -> monitor.
researcher_notes: NOT matched_existing: distinct from P3657 (Israel-Egypt Offshore, an Israel->Egypt Leviathan/Tamar export concept, 6.7 bcm, different origin/sponsor) and from P5276 (Israel->Gaza supply, opposite direction; not in the Egypt roster). Gaza Marine is a separate ~28-30 bcm field in Palestinian waters, ~35 km offshore Gaza, discovered 2000. The Egyptian development option: ~50-60 km (~40-mile) subsea line delivering Gaza Marine gas to the Egyptian grid at El Arish for processing, with in-system swap for Idku LNG export. Confidence tier MEDIUM: two independent sources agree on the core facts (MESP long-form 2024-02; Middle East Eye 2022-10), corroborated by MEES, Egypt Oil & Gas, and Wikipedia 'Natural gas in the Gaza Strip' — but they are largely secondary/analytical and there is no primary pipeline milestone (no route, no FEED/EPC, no tender). Ownership stakes (EGAS 45% / PIF 27.5% / CCC 27.5%) and Cheiron as EGAS technical lead are consistently reported. Route: no defined corridor; would be an offshore Gaza->Sinai coast line, but nothing GIS-grade exists. Recommend MONITOR for a pipeline-specific milestone (route defined, FEED/EPC award, or tender) before creating a GEM row; revisit if Gaza-war ceasefire revives field development.
